Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ১) In a typical adult male, total body water (TBW) is approximately.......... of body weight?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
In a typical adult male, total body water (TBW) is approximately 60% of body weight.

For a 70 kg adult male:

TBW ≈ 70 × 0.6 = 42 L

TBW distribution:

  • Intracellular fluid (ICF) → 2/3 of TBW

  • Extracellular fluid (ECF) → 1/3 of TBW

Exam pearl:
“Adult male TBW ≈ 60% of body weight.”

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ২) Following electrolyte imbalance occurs after vomiting except....?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
Vomiting causes loss of gastric HCl, resulting in metabolic alkalosis, not metabolic acidosis.

Typical electrolyte/acid–base changes after prolonged vomiting:

  • Hyponatremia → may occur

  • Hypokalemia → common

  • Metabolic alkalosis → characteristic

  • Metabolic acidosis → not typical

Exam pearl:
“Vomiting → loss of H⁺/Cl⁻ → hypochloremic, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis.”

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ৩) Which is not a sign of atropinization?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
Atropinization means achieving adequate atropine effect, classically in organophosphate poisoning. The important signs include:

  • Clear chest on auscultation → reduction of bronchial secretions

  • Dry axilla/skin → decreased sweating

  • Heart rate >80/min → correction of excessive vagal activity

  • Pupillary dilatation (mydriasis) may occur

Pinpoint pupil (miosis) is instead a feature of organophosphate poisoning, not atropinization.

Exam pearl:
“Atropinization → dry + clear chest + adequate HR + dilating pupils.”

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ৪) Which is a feature of fluid overload?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
Fluid overload causes increased hydrostatic pressure and fluid accumulation in tissues and body cavities. Pleural effusion is a typical feature.

  • Pleural effusion → fluid overload

  • Postural hypotension → usually volume depletion

  • Tachycardia → more typical of hypovolemia

  • Low JVP → suggests volume depletion

  • Fluid overload → raised JVP, peripheral edema, pulmonary edema/pleural effusion

Exam pearl:
“Fluid overload → raised JVP + edema + pleural effusion.”

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ৫) What is the choice of fluid in diarrhoea?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
For diarrhoeal dehydration, the preferred oral rehydration fluid is ORS (oral rehydration solution). In traditional exam terminology, “cholera saline” refers to an oral rehydration solution used to replace water and electrolytes lost through diarrhea.

  • Cholera saline → ORS for diarrhoeal dehydration

  • Normal saline → mainly used IV when indicated

  • Hartmann’s solution → IV fluid, useful in severe dehydration/shock

  • “Diarrhoea saline” → not the standard term

Exam pearl:
“Diarrhoea → ORS (cholera saline).”

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ৬) Which of the following is a cause of normal anion gap metabolic acidosis?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
Diarrhoea causes loss of bicarbonate (HCO₃⁻) from the gastrointestinal tract, resulting in normal anion gap (hyperchloremic) metabolic acidosis.

  • Diarrhoea → normal anion gap metabolic acidosis

  • DKA → high anion gap metabolic acidosis

  • Renal failure → usually high anion gap metabolic acidosis in advanced disease

  • Aspirin poisoning → high anion gap metabolic acidosis (often with respiratory alkalosis)

Exam pearl:
“Normal AG metabolic acidosis = HCO₃⁻ loss → think diarrhoea.”

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ৭) What is the cause of euvolemic hyponatremia?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone secretion) is the classic cause of euvolemic hyponatremia. Excess ADH causes water retention, but the body compensates with increased renal sodium excretion, so there is no significant edema or volume depletion.

  • SIADH → euvolemic hyponatremia

  • Diuretics → commonly hypovolemic hyponatremia

  • CCF → hypervolemic hyponatremia

  • CRF → usually hypervolemic hyponatremia

Exam pearl:
“Euvolemic hyponatremia → think SIADH.”

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ৮) Tetany may occur in....?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
Tetany can occur in alkalosis, particularly acute respiratory alkalosis. Increased blood pH increases the binding of calcium to albumin, reducing ionized Ca²⁺, which increases neuromuscular excitability and can cause carpopedal spasm and tetany.

  • Alkalosis → ↓ ionized Ca²⁺ → tetany

  • Acidosis → usually increases ionized Ca²⁺

  • Hypokalemia → muscle weakness/cramps, not classic tetany

  • Hyponatremia → neurological symptoms, not typical tetany

Exam pearl:
“Alkalosis → ↓ ionized calcium → tetany.”

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ৯) What is the choice of treatment in moderate hyponatremia?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
In moderate hyponatremia, particularly when associated with hypovolemia, 0.9% normal saline (NaCl) is commonly used to restore circulating volume and correct the sodium abnormality.

  • 0.9% NaCl → appropriate for hypovolemic hyponatremia

  • 3% NaCl → reserved for severe/symptomatic hyponatremia, especially with neurological symptoms

  • Oral salt/tablets → may be used in selected chronic cases, depending on the cause

Exam pearl:
“Moderate hypovolemic hyponatremia → 0.9% NaCl.”

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ১০) Atropine is antidote for which type of poisoning?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
Atropine is a major antidote for organophosphorus (OPC) poisoning. It competitively blocks muscarinic acetylcholine receptors, reversing muscarinic effects such as:

  • Excessive salivation

  • Bronchorrhea

  • Bronchospasm

  • Bradycardia

  • Lacrimation

Pralidoxime (2-PAM) is also used in organophosphate poisoning to reactivate acetylcholinesterase, particularly when given early.

Exam pearl:
“OPC poisoning → Atropine + Pralidoxime.”

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ১১) What is the cause of hypervolemic hyponatremia?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
Hypervolemic hyponatremia occurs when there is excess total body water and sodium, but the increase in water is proportionally greater. Chronic renal failure (CRF/CKD) can cause impaired water excretion, leading to water retention and dilutional hyponatremia.

  • CRF → hypervolemic hyponatremia

  • SIADH → euvolemic hyponatremia

  • Diuretics → usually hypovolemic hyponatremia

  • Diabetes insipidus → hypernatremia due to water loss

Exam pearl:
“Hypervolemic hyponatremia → think CKD/CRF, CCF, cirrhosis.”

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ১২) Which isn't included in acute management of OPC poisoning?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
The acute management of organophosphorus compound (OPC) poisoning includes:

  • Atropine → reverses muscarinic effects

  • Pralidoxime (2-PAM) → reactivates acetylcholinesterase, especially when given early

  • Gastric decontamination/lavage → may be considered in selected cases with appropriate airway protection

Dialysis is not a routine treatment for OPC poisoning.

Exam pearl:
“OPC poisoning → Atropine + Pralidoxime + supportive/decontamination measures; dialysis is not routine.”

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ১৩) Which ECG change occurs in hypokalemia?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
The characteristic ECG change in hypokalemia is a prominent U wave, best seen in the precordial leads (V2–V3).

  • Hypokalemia → prominent U wave, flattened T wave, ST depression

  • Hyperkalemia → tall peaked T wave, widened QRS, loss of P wave

Exam pearl:
“Hypokalemia → U wave.”

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ১৪) Which drug is used to stabilize cell membrane in hyperkalemia?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
IV calcium gluconate is used in significant hyperkalemia with ECG changes to stabilize the cardiac cell membrane. It acts rapidly but does not lower serum potassium.

  • Calcium gluconate → stabilizes cardiac membrane

  • Insulin + glucose → shifts K⁺ into cells

  • Salbutamol → shifts K⁺ intracellularly

  • Frusemide → increases renal K⁺ excretion

Exam pearl:
“Hyperkalemia + ECG changes → IV calcium gluconate for membrane stabilization.”

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ১৫) Which is not a phase of OPC poisoning?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
Organophosphate (OPC) poisoning has three recognized clinical phases:

  1. Acute cholinergic syndrome → occurs soon after exposure due to excess acetylcholine.

  2. Intermediate syndrome (IMS) → develops typically 24–96 hours after acute poisoning and causes proximal/respiratory muscle weakness.

  3. Organophosphate-induced delayed polyneuropathy (OPIDN) → develops 1–3 weeks after exposure, causing predominantly distal weakness and sensory symptoms.

“Chronic cholinergic syndrome” is not a recognized phase of OPC poisoning.

Exam pearl:
OPC phases = Acute cholinergic syndrome → Intermediate syndrome → Delayed polyneuropathy.

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ১৬) Hyperkalemia is associated with which of the following?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
Acidosis can cause hyperkalemia because H⁺ moves into cells and K⁺ shifts out of cells, increasing serum potassium.

  • Acidosis → K⁺ shifts out of cells → hyperkalemia

  • Alkalosis → K⁺ shifts into cells → hypokalemia

Exam pearl:
“Acidosis → Hyperkalemia; Alkalosis → Hypokalemia.”

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ১৭) Triad of tetany excludes which of the following?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
The classic triad of tetany includes:

  • Carpopedal spasm

  • Stridor/laryngospasm

  • Convulsions

Coma is not a component of the classic tetany triad.

Exam pearl:
“Tetany triad = Carpopedal spasm + Stridor + Convulsion.”

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ১৮) OPC acts on which enzyme?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
Organophosphorus compounds (OPC) inhibit acetylcholinesterase (AChE), causing accumulation of acetylcholine at cholinergic synapses.

This produces the characteristic cholinergic symptoms such as salivation, lacrimation, bronchorrhea, bronchospasm, vomiting, diarrhea, and bradycardia.

  • OPC → inhibits acetylcholinesterase

  • ↑ Acetylcholine → cholinergic toxicity

Exam pearl:
“OPC poisoning = Acetylcholinesterase inhibition.”

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ১৯) What is the basic daily sodium requirements in a normal adult person?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
The basic daily sodium requirement for a normal adult is approximately 100–140 mmol/day according to the conventional exam-based value.

  • 100–140 mmol/day → normal adult sodium requirement

  • Sodium is essential for ECF volume, osmotic balance, nerve conduction, and muscle function.

Exam pearl:
“Daily Na⁺ requirement ≈ 100–140 mmol/day.”

Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.question: ২০) Rapid correction of hyponatremia with 3% NaCl may lead to.......?
Water and Electrolytes and Acid-base Hom.exp:
Rapid correction of chronic hyponatremia, especially with hypertonic 3% NaCl, can cause osmotic demyelination syndrome (ODS), classically central pontine myelinolysis.

  • Rapid Na⁺ correction → osmotic demyelination

  • Central pontine myelinolysis → classic manifestation

  • Can cause dysarthria, dysphagia, quadriparesis, altered consciousness, and severe neurological deficits.

Exam pearl:
“Rapid correction of hyponatremia → Central pontine myelinolysis.”
